# Verify in production

A change is finished when someone has watched it work. Most changes you can watch **now**, and
that is the rule — this skill is only for the rest: a change whose proof lives somewhere the
repo cannot see yet. You are filing the proof, not doing the work — and the proof itself runs
unattended: an automatic check, end to end, with a person entering
only where no automatic check can exist.

## When it fires: after the merge, never before

**The PR must have merged.** This skill runs as a step of the merge, unasked — `merge-to-main`
calls it once the squash has landed — and at no other moment. Not when the code is written, not
when the PR opens, not while review is in flight.

The reason is that a PR can be **rejected**, and a branch that is still open can be rewritten
under you. Both leave a verification whose premise never reached `main`:

- A **rewritten branch** makes the brief describe a change that no longer exists. #1121 was filed
  against a scope its PR then dropped; the verification was moot before the merge it waited on.
- A **rejected PR** is worse, because the queue cannot tell it from a merge. A blocked item
  releases on its blocker being *closed*, and nothing reads `merged` — so the item goes ready,
  reads an `In-production-when:` that can never become true, pushes `Not-before:` forward by
  `Retry-every:` without comment, and repeats indefinitely. No janitor rule reclaims it: the
  stale-ready sweep cannot see an item sleeping on a future `Not-before`, and the
  stuck-dependency sweep exempts an item whose blockers have closed.

So there is no such thing as filing this early and letting the queue sort it out. Wait for the
merge, then read **what actually landed** — the merged diff, not the branch you remember writing.

## First: does this file anything at all?

Most changes **file nothing.** Run the test in this order and stop at the first answer:

1. **Did you watch it work in this session?** Then it is proven. File nothing.
2. **Did a test that ran prove it?** A unit test, a CI job, an executable-requirements or UI
   test covering exactly the behaviour that changed. File nothing — the suite is the mechanism
   that comes back.
3. **Does the change have an observable effect at all?** A comment, a design doc, a README, a
   rename with no behavioural edge, a refactor a passing suite already pins. File nothing.
4. **Otherwise: where does its effect first become observable?** If the answer is a place and a
   moment — a member repo once it converges, a site once it deploys, a session once it reloads
   its rules — that is what you file.

The bar is *could not be watched now*, not *would be nice to double-check*. A verification
filed for a change already covered by a test is a wasted run re-proving what the suite proved.

## What you file

**A deferred request** — the same ad-hoc lane `/do-later` rides, so the queue does the waiting,
the running and the lifecycle; nothing here adds machinery beside it. One issue, titled
`Verify in production: <the change, in a few words>`, its body the whole brief: the run that
verifies will never see this conversation and may be days away. Say what changed and why it
could not be watched now, then, each spelled verbatim on its own line:

```
Original-issue: #<the change's issue>
In-production-when: <the concrete artifact to read, and what makes it true>
Verify: <what to observe, and what counts as a pass>
Not-before: <ISO instant just past the expected release>
Retry-every: <how far to push Not-before when not yet live, e.g. 1 day>
```

No `Blocked-by:`. You are filing after the merge, so the change's PR has already closed and
there is nothing left to wait on but the release itself.

- **`Original-issue:`** is where a failure lands — the issue the change was done under, which
  the run reopens if the verification fails. Make the verification that issue's **sub-issue**
  too (`mcp__github__sub_issue_write`, method `add`, `issue_number` the original,
  `sub_issue_id` the **id** the create call returned, not its number), so the change it proves
  shows what is still unproven about it — [RULES.md](../../RULES.md)' *Filing an issue that
  belongs under another*, applied where there is no PR left to carry the link.
- **`In-production-when:`** names a thing to *read*, never a duration to wait. "`missingbulb/Shepherd`'s
  `.claudinite-checks.json` stamps `packVersions.tidy-repo` at 8 or higher." "The live site's
  `/version.json` reports a version past 4.2.0." "Any session started after this landed — check
  the vendored copy under `.claudinite/shared/` carries the new text." A merge is not a
  production condition, and neither is elapsed time.
- **`Verify:`** is an assertion with a pass condition, not a topic — and a read an **unattended
  run can make**: an API response, a file at a URL, an issue's state. "Issue #100 on that repo
  is closed with a comment citing the scheduler runs" beats "check tidy-issues works". Only where no
  automatic check can exist may `Verify:` name a person's step, spelled out exactly.
- **`Not-before:`** is the queue's own wait field: adoption holds the run until the moment has
  passed. Aim it just past the release you expect — the re-arm covers a miss, so don't pad it.
- **`Retry-every:`** is the extension you are prescribing: when the run finds the change not
  yet live, it pushes `Not-before:` forward by exactly this much. Size it to the release you
  wait on — a nightly converge retries daily, a next-session rule in minutes.

Then the mark, as `/do-later` applies it: **`task:origin:ad-hoc`**, the one label the scheduler
run adopts. Beside it, in the body, **`Model: sonnet`** (reading a live artifact and judging an
assertion against it). Never `Automerge:` — a verification has nothing to merge. If the mark
doesn't exist in the repo yet, say so and leave the issue — it appears on the next scheduler run.

## Tell the run how to converge

End the body with instructions to the run itself — the issue is its whole brief, and the run
decides nothing: it executes this playbook.

1. Read `In-production-when:` against the real artifact. Never infer it from a merge, a green
   run, or elapsed time.
2. **Live** → run `Verify:`. Passes: comment the evidence actually read (the version, the value,
   the URL) and close this issue as completed. Fails: reopen `Original-issue:` with a comment
   saying what was asserted, what happened instead and where you read it; comment here linking
   that; close this issue as completed — the verification did its job by finding the fault.
3. **Not yet live** → push `Not-before:` forward by `Retry-every:`, **clear the issue's
   `task:status:*` label** (clearing the status is the whole of the re-ask — the mark stays on
   for life), and leave the issue open. The next scheduler run re-adopts it, and the bumped
   field holds it until the new moment. No comment; the bumped field is the record.

## Then say what you filed

One line back to the owner: the issue link, what it waits on, and its retry cadence.

input.body:
#25 landed hitbut v1 (PR #29). Everything in it is proven by cases that ran — 44 leaves across four lanes, green locally and on CI — with exactly one exception, and this issue is that exception coming back on its own instead of waiting on anyone's memory.

Requirement `7.1`, *"a merge to `main` reaches the deployed site with no human build step"*, is the one leaf in `dev/requirements/provisional.json`: it is a claim about a live Cloudflare account, and no test in this repository can observe it. The deploy job exists and is wired (`.github/workflows/product.yml` → `ship main`: apply the D1 migrations, deploy the Worker, build the site against the deployed API, deploy the Pages project), but until provisioning (#27) lands it detects the missing credentials, says so, and exits clean — so a green `main` today says nothing about shipping.

Model: sonnet

```
Original-issue: #25
In-production-when: the most recent completed run of the `product` workflow on `main` has a `ship main` job whose conclusion is `success` (while provisioning is outstanding it concludes `skipped`, which is not this condition)
Verify: take the Worker origin and the Pages URL from that run (its `Deploy the Worker` and `Deploy the site` step logs print both; the `API_ORIGIN` repository variable holds the Worker origin, and #27 records what was created). Then: `GET <worker-origin>/api/v1/figures` returns 200 with a JSON body whose `items` is an array, and `GET <pages-url>/` returns 200 HTML containing `התבטאויות`. Pass = both hold. Anything else — a 404, an empty `items`, an HTML error page, a 5xx — is a fail, and `GET <worker-origin>/api/v1/nope` returning 404 with `{"error":{"code":"not_found"}}` confirms it is our Worker answering rather than a platform placeholder
Not-before: 2026-08-28T09:00:00Z
Retry-every: 1 week
```

A week's retry is sized to what this waits on: a person working through #27's checklist in a dashboard, on no schedule. It will re-arm quietly until they do.

## What the run does

1. Read `In-production-when:` against the Actions API. Never infer it from a merge, a green run, or elapsed time — the deploy job is *designed* to go green while doing nothing.
2. **Live** → run `Verify:`. Passes: comment the evidence actually read (both URLs and what they returned) and close this issue as completed. Fails: reopen #25 with a comment saying what was asserted, what happened instead and where it was read; comment here linking that; close this issue as completed — finding the fault is the job.
3. **Not yet live** → push `Not-before:` forward by one week, clear the issue's `task:status:*` label, and leave it open. No comment; the bumped field is the record.

When this passes, two other things become true and are worth doing in the same change: `7.1` comes off `dev/requirements/provisional.json` (it can be claimed by a real case once there is a deployment to assert against), and the first gap in #28 shrinks to what a local `workerd` still cannot tell you about Cloudflare's.

{"id":5215350096,"number":25,"state":"closed","state_reason":"completed","locked":false,"title":"Implement hitbut v1: corpus, analysis, API, site","body":"The tracking issue for building hitbut v1. **No implementation has started** — this issue is the plan, filed from the bootstrap session (#22). The mechanism (what each piece *is* and why) lives in [`docs/architecture/DESIGN.md`](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/blob/main/docs/architecture/DESIGN.md) (landed via PR #23); this issue carries only the phases and their exit conditions. The visual target for the site is the design canvas: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/a6544164-7a52-48c0-835a-aace6bd3569a (home, figure page, inconsistency page, mobile, plus two alternate directions — all sample data fictional).

Once the plan is agreed the body is append-only: check boxes, add below, never rewrite.

## Decisions the owner must make before phase 2

These gate the build; everything in phases 0–1 is decision-free.

- [x] **Scope of figures and sources for v1.** Which public figures, which jurisdiction, and which 2–3 first sources? The safest corpus backbone is official/government transcript sources (no ToS exposure, no platform API to be killed by); the market-landscape wiki's legal findings that inform this need owner promotion into `product-wiki/product-requirements/` before the spec may cite them.
- [x] **Alternate design direction check.** The canvas commits to "warm editorial"; two alternates (civic data-first, stark contrast) sit beside it. Approve a direction (editing the canvas counts).
- [x] **Frontend stack.** DESIGN.md fixes "static assets, no server rendering"; the framework (vanilla + a router, Preact, Svelte…) is open. Recommendation: smallest thing that renders API JSON — decide at phase 7, not before.
- [x] **Product name/domain confirmation** ("hitbut" as public brand, or working title only?).

## Phases

**0. Cloudflare provisioning (out-of-band setup, front-loaded)**
- [ ] Cloudflare account: create D1 database, R2 bucket, Queue, Workers project, Pages project; store a scoped API token in repo secrets for CI deploys.
- [ ] Exit: a CI dry-run (`wrangler deploy --dry-run` + `wrangler pages project list`) passes against the committed `wrangler` config.
- When implementation starts, the human-only steps here get their own checklist issue per the basics hand-over rule; nothing later in this plan may precede this phase.

**1. Executable-requirements harness**
- [ ] `dev/requirements/requirements.md` authored from the adoption answers (product/users/market) — numbered leaves, one-line scannable, detail in `<details>`.
- [ ] Coverage gate (bijection: every leaf ⇄ exactly one case of the right kind), kind folders (`logic`, `behavior`, `server`, `screen`), runners, CI wiring. Watch the gate fail (doc-first red-by-default) before the first case lands.
- [ ] Exit: CI runs the gate; non-zero test count; gate green with the initial leaf set claimed.

**2. Shared contract (`src/shared/`)**
- [ ] Types for `Figure`, `Source`, `Statement`, `Inconsistency` and the `/api/v1` request/response shapes, per DESIGN.md's data model (stable ids, null-not-defaulted unknowns).
- [ ] Exit: both sides import only from `src/shared`; barrier check green.

**3. Corpus store (`src/backend/corpus/`)**
- [ ] D1 schema + migrations; FTS index; id assignment (figure slugs, statement/inconsistency ULIDs); retirement-as-status invariants.
- [ ] Exit: logic-kind cases prove id stability, unknown-date handling, and supersede-not-delete; green in CI.

**4. Acquisition (`src/backend/acquisition/`)**
- [ ] One shared fetch module (retries, backoff, bot-wall detection, raw-to-R2 before parse) and the per-source module registry (declared surface, refresh clock, extractor).
- [ ] First two owner-approved sources, each proven against a committed real captured sample with owner-reviewed expected values (the supported-targets-matrix discipline).
- [ ] Exit: cron dry-run over fixtures produces statement records byte-stable across two runs; per-source cases green.

**5. Analysis (`src/backend/analysis/`)**
- [ ] Queue consumer; candidate pairing (same figure ∩ overlapping topics); LLM judgment behind one interface; committed versioned prompt; full score retention with a surfacing threshold; every record carries both statement ids + rationale + model/prompt version.
- [ ] Exit: behavior-kind cases over fixture pairs (a known contradiction, a known consistent pair, a position shift) produce the expected kinds and store the full trail; re-analysis supersedes, never overwrites.

**6. HTTP API (`src/backend/api/`)**
- [ ] `/api/v1`: figures, figure timeline, statement, inconsistencies, search; cursor pagination; open CORS; read-only. Bulk NDJSON export generated to R2.
- [ ] Exit: server-kind cases against the real handler under `wrangler dev`; contract types round-trip.

**7. Frontend (`src/frontend/`)**
- [ ] The six pages from the design canvas (home, figure, statement, inconsistency, search, methodology) against `/api/v1`; the methodology page states the honest-gap sentence (what detection confirms vs. what it cannot).
- [ ] Exit: screen-kind Playwright goldens per UI leaf, owner-reviewed, green against a local preview of the real deployment.

**8. Ship-on-green**
- [ ] `wrangler` deploy of Workers + Pages from `main` on its own cadence; red `main` is a shipping outage.
- [ ] Exit: a change merged to `main` reaches the deployed site with no human build step, observed once end-to-end.

Ordering: 0 → 1 → 2 → 3 → {4, 5, 6 in any order — 5 and 6 depend on 3; 4 feeds 5 via the queue} → 7 → 8. Review lands as one stack per the plans discipline, not a wait per phase.

## Explicitly out of v1

Watchlists/alerts (segment 4), accounts, non-English sources, deleted-statement tracking, any paid tier. Each is a later issue when the corpus exists.

---

## Decisions recorded (2026-08-21)

Owner answered all four (bootstrap session, #22):

1. **v1 scope: Israeli politicians, journalists and commentators.** Statements mostly in Hebrew, but not exclusively. (This supersedes the "non-English sources" exclusion above — Hebrew is the primary language, and "out of v1" now means no *additional* languages beyond Hebrew and English.)
2. **Design direction: warm editorial**, as built on the canvas.
3. **Frontend stack: Preact + Vite.**
4. **"hitbut" is the public brand.**

### What the Israeli/Hebrew scope changes, at the phase where each lands

- **Sources (phase 4):** the official-transcript backbone becomes Knesset plenum and committee protocols plus gov.il announcements; journalists/commentators imply Israeli press and broadcast sources. Each candidate source gets a `map-a-data-source` recon before any parser; the owner still picks the first 2–3 concrete sources from that recon.
- **Language (phases 3, 5):** `Statement` carries a language field. D1/SQLite FTS default tokenizers handle Hebrew morphology poorly (agglutinated prefixes ה/ו/ב/ל/מ/ש), so search needs a Hebrew-aware tokenization strategy, proven with logic-kind cases over Hebrew fixtures. The analysis model must be strong in Hebrew — DESIGN.md's "v1 binds to Workers AI" must be re-evaluated for Hebrew competence before phase 5 (the planned one-interface isolation makes a swap config-level; DESIGN.md gets a PR when that call is made).
- **RTL + typography (phase 7):** the site is RTL-first with LTR support for non-Hebrew statements. The canvas's Newsreader/Public Sans carry no Hebrew glyphs — Hebrew families needed (e.g. Frank Ruhl Libre serif + Heebo/Assistant sans) and a mirrored layout; the "but" badge presumably becomes «אבל». The canvas gets an RTL/Hebrew pass before phase-7 goldens are cut.
- **Legal (owner review, before launch):** the market-landscape wiki's legal findings are US-only; Israeli defamation law (חוק איסור לשון הרע) is materially stricter, and the disclosed-facts-opinion posture needs checking against it. {"id":5215350096,"number":25,"state":"closed","state_reason":"completed","locked":false,"title":"Implement hitbut v1: corpus, analysis, API, site","body":"The tracking issue for building hitbut v1. **No implementation has started** — this issue is the plan, filed from the bootstrap session (#22). The mechanism (what each piece *is* and why) lives in [`docs/architecture/DESIGN.md`](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/blob/main/docs/architecture/DESIGN.md) (landed via PR #23); this issue carries only the phases and their exit conditions. The visual target for the site is the design canvas: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/a6544164-7a52-48c0-835a-aace6bd3569a (home, figure page, inconsistency page, mobile, plus two alternate directions — all sample data fictional).

Once the plan is agreed the body is append-only: check boxes, add below, never rewrite.

## Decisions the owner must make before phase 2

These gate the build; everything in phases 0–1 is decision-free.

- [x] **Scope of figures and sources for v1.** Which public figures, which jurisdiction, and which 2–3 first sources? The safest corpus backbone is official/government transcript sources (no ToS exposure, no platform API to be killed by); the market-landscape wiki's legal findings that inform this need owner promotion into `product-wiki/product-requirements/` before the spec may cite them.
- [x] **Alternate design direction check.** The canvas commits to "warm editorial"; two alternates (civic data-first, stark contrast) sit beside it. Approve a direction (editing the canvas counts).
- [x] **Frontend stack.** DESIGN.md fixes "static assets, no server rendering"; the framework (vanilla + a router, Preact, Svelte…) is open. Recommendation: smallest thing that renders API JSON — decide at phase 7, not before.
- [x] **Product name/domain confirmation** ("hitbut" as public brand, or working title only?).

## Phases

**0. Cloudflare provisioning (out-of-band setup, front-loaded)**
- [ ] Cloudflare account: create D1 database, R2 bucket, Queue, Workers project, Pages project; store a scoped API token in repo secrets for CI deploys.
- [ ] Exit: a CI dry-run (`wrangler deploy --dry-run` + `wrangler pages project list`) passes against the committed `wrangler` config.
- When implementation starts, the human-only steps here get their own checklist issue per the basics hand-over rule; nothing later in this plan may precede this phase.

**1. Executable-requirements harness**
- [ ] `dev/requirements/requirements.md` authored from the adoption answers (product/users/market) — numbered leaves, one-line scannable, detail in `<details>`.
- [ ] Coverage gate (bijection: every leaf ⇄ exactly one case of the right kind), kind folders (`logic`, `behavior`, `server`, `screen`), runners, CI wiring. Watch the gate fail (doc-first red-by-default) before the first case lands.
- [ ] Exit: CI runs the gate; non-zero test count; gate green with the initial leaf set claimed.

**2. Shared contract (`src/shared/`)**
- [ ] Types for `Figure`, `Source`, `Statement`, `Inconsistency` and the `/api/v1` request/response shapes, per DESIGN.md's data model (stable ids, null-not-defaulted unknowns).
- [ ] Exit: both sides import only from `src/shared`; barrier check green.

**3. Corpus store (`src/backend/corpus/`)**
- [ ] D1 schema + migrations; FTS index; id assignment (figure slugs, statement/inconsistency ULIDs); retirement-as-status invariants.
- [ ] Exit: logic-kind cases prove id stability, unknown-date handling, and supersede-not-delete; green in CI.

**4. Acquisition (`src/backend/acquisition/`)**
- [ ] One shared fetch module (retries, backoff, bot-wall detection, raw-to-R2 before parse) and the per-source module registry (declared surface, refresh clock, extractor).
- [ ] First two owner-approved sources, each proven against a committed real captured sample with owner-reviewed expected values (the supported-targets-matrix discipline).
- [ ] Exit: cron dry-run over fixtures produces statement records byte-stable across two runs; per-source cases green.

**5. Analysis (`src/backend/analysis/`)**
- [ ] Queue consumer; candidate pairing (same figure ∩ overlapping topics); LLM judgment behind one interface; committed versioned prompt; full score retention with a surfacing threshold; every record carries both statement ids + rationale + model/prompt version.
- [ ] Exit: behavior-kind cases over fixture pairs (a known contradiction, a known consistent pair, a position shift) produce the expected kinds and store the full trail; re-analysis supersedes, never overwrites.

**6. HTTP API (`src/backend/api/`)**
- [ ] `/api/v1`: figures, figure timeline, statement, inconsistencies, search; cursor pagination; open CORS; read-only. Bulk NDJSON export generated to R2.
- [ ] Exit: server-kind cases against the real handler under `wrangler dev`; contract types round-trip.

**7. Frontend (`src/frontend/`)**
- [ ] The six pages from the design canvas (home, figure, statement, inconsistency, search, methodology) against `/api/v1`; the methodology page states the honest-gap sentence (what detection confirms vs. what it cannot).
- [ ] Exit: screen-kind Playwright goldens per UI leaf, owner-reviewed, green against a local preview of the real deployment.

**8. Ship-on-green**
- [ ] `wrangler` deploy of Workers + Pages from `main` on its own cadence; red `main` is a shipping outage.
- [ ] Exit: a change merged to `main` reaches the deployed site with no human build step, observed once end-to-end.

Ordering: 0 → 1 → 2 → 3 → {4, 5, 6 in any order — 5 and 6 depend on 3; 4 feeds 5 via the queue} → 7 → 8. Review lands as one stack per the plans discipline, not a wait per phase.

## Explicitly out of v1

Watchlists/alerts (segment 4), accounts, non-English sources, deleted-statement tracking, any paid tier. Each is a later issue when the corpus exists.

---

## Decisions recorded (2026-08-21)

Owner answered all four (bootstrap session, #22):

1. **v1 scope: Israeli politicians, journalists and commentators.** Statements mostly in Hebrew, but not exclusively. (This supersedes the "non-English sources" exclusion above — Hebrew is the primary language, and "out of v1" now means no *additional* languages beyond Hebrew and English.)
2. **Design direction: warm editorial**, as built on the canvas.
3. **Frontend stack: Preact + Vite.**
4. **"hitbut" is the public brand.**

### What the Israeli/Hebrew scope changes, at the phase where each lands

- **Sources (phase 4):** the official-transcript backbone becomes Knesset plenum and committee protocols plus gov.il announcements; journalists/commentators imply Israeli press and broadcast sources. Each candidate source gets a `map-a-data-source` recon before any parser; the owner still picks the first 2–3 concrete sources from that recon.
- **Language (phases 3, 5):** `Statement` carries a language field. D1/SQLite FTS default tokenizers handle Hebrew morphology poorly (agglutinated prefixes ה/ו/ב/ל/מ/ש), so search needs a Hebrew-aware tokenization strategy, proven with logic-kind cases over Hebrew fixtures. The analysis model must be strong in Hebrew — DESIGN.md's "v1 binds to Workers AI" must be re-evaluated for Hebrew competence before phase 5 (the planned one-interface isolation makes a swap config-level; DESIGN.md gets a PR when that call is made).
- **RTL + typography (phase 7):** the site is RTL-first with LTR support for non-Hebrew statements. The canvas's Newsreader/Public Sans carry no Hebrew glyphs — Hebrew families needed (e.g. Frank Ruhl Libre serif + Heebo/Assistant sans) and a mirrored layout; the "but" badge presumably becomes «אבל». The canvas gets an RTL/Hebrew pass before phase-7 goldens are cut.
- **Legal (owner review, before launch):** the market-landscape wiki's legal findings are US-only; Israeli defamation law (חוק איסור לשון הרע) is materially stricter, and the disclosed-facts-opinion posture needs checking against it. === product-wiki/market-landscape/README.md ===
## Key insights

- Fact-checking has peaked: ~443 orgs worldwide, output down ~6%, and 76% describe their finances as vulnerable or in crisis
- Meta and USAID — the field's two biggest funders — both vanished for US-facing work within six months in 2025
- Google killed the fact-check search snippet in June 2025, so distribution collapsed the same year as funding
- Community Notes measurably works — reposts of noted posts drop 46% — so the crowd model is a real substitute, not just cover
- The closest product already shipped: Factba.se indexes presidents' every word; sold to FiscalNote, now lives inside Roll Call
- PR teams pay $10k–40k/yr for media monitoring, but policy-intelligence leader FiscalNote is shrinking 21%/yr
- Courts protect verdict-style labels as opinion when sources are disclosed; scraping risk is contract/ToS, not criminal law

## Public fact-checking: a field at its plateau, hit by a double funding shock
=== product-wiki/competitor-landscape/README.md ===
## Key insights

- PolitiFact has tracked flip-flops since 2008 (Flip-O-Meter) — but editorial, case-by-case; no browsable per-figure corpus
- Nobody ships a per-figure statement timeline; C-SPAN's person pages come closest, and C-SPAN is in financial crisis
- The X/Twitter API shutdown killed both politician-tweet archives (Politwoops, PolitiTweet) — platform dependence is the top cause of death
- Full Fact already runs AI that alerts when an MP repeats a debunked claim — the closest live tech to automated inconsistency detection
- WaPo's 30,573-claim Trump database was frozen in Jan 2021 and never restarted; its editor left in 2025 with no successor named
- Commercial monitors (Meltwater, Cision, NewsWhip) sell private alerts to PR teams, not public per-figure histories — the niche is open
- No project found that combines a scraped sourced corpus, automated contradiction detection, and public per-figure browsing

Confirmed two things worth knowing before I answer.

**The sandbox can't reach any of the candidate sources.** `knesset.gov.il`, `gov.il` and `oknesset.org` are all denied at the proxy — `403` on CONNECT, a policy denial rather than a bot wall. So no reconnaissance happens from a session; it needs a sanctioned home on a runner.

**And the code has no notion of a roster.** A figure is minted by `ensureFigure` the moment any extractor names a speaker — so today the tracked-persons list *is* whatever the sources happen to contain. That's backwards for this product, and it's the first thing to fix.

input.title: Seed the figure roster explicitly — an unknown speaker must not become a tracked figure
input.body:
Today `runAcquisition` calls `ensureFigure({ displayName: raw.speaker.displayName, ... })` for every speaker an extractor names, and `ensureFigure` creates the figure if the name is new. The roster is therefore a *byproduct* of what got crawled. Two things follow, and both are wrong for this product:

**1. Anyone named in a document becomes a tracked public figure.** A committee protocol names witnesses, petitioners, private citizens giving testimony, clerks. Each of them would get a slug, a page, and a timeline — and eventually an inconsistency flag. That is precisely the exposure the market-landscape wiki's legal section is about, and Israeli defamation law is stricter than the US law that section surveys. It is a defect, not a policy choice.

**2. Coverage becomes unknowable.** Requirement `5.10` makes an unknown figure a 404 rather than an empty 200, for good reasons. But a figure who exists with a thin timeline is the same problem one step in: a reader cannot tell "this is their record" from "this is the part of their record we happen to have crawled". A roster we chose lets the page say which sources and which period it covers; a roster we stumbled into cannot.

## The shape of the fix

- A **committed roster** is an input to acquisition, not an output of it: who we track, why they qualify, and which sources cover them.
- An extracted statement whose speaker is not on the roster is **not dropped and not promoted** — it is stored unattributed (or against a `pending` figure) so the raw record stays complete and a person can decide. Unknown is its own state here too.
- `ensureFigure` stops being reachable from the acquisition path; adding a figure becomes a reviewed change.
- The roster carries an **inclusion rule** — the written test a person must meet to be tracked — and the methodology page publishes it. For elected officials the rule is trivial; for commentators it is the whole of the defensibility, and an arbitrary list is the thing to avoid.
- A figure page states its coverage: which sources, from when.

## Requirements this adds

Doc-first, so these are leaves before they are code — under §1 (identifiers and the corpus):

- a speaker not on the roster does not create a figure
- a statement by an unrecognised speaker is retained, unattributed, rather than dropped
- a figure page states the sources and period its record covers

Not started; filed from the seeding discussion so it is not carried in anyone's head. It should land **before** the first real source does, because the first crawl is exactly when an unrostered speaker first appears.

Refs #25

Here's how I'd seed it.

## The principle: seed the people, discover the statements

The roster is an editorial decision and should be a committed input; the statements are what crawling is for. Getting this backwards is what [#31](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/31) is about — and it wants fixing before the first real source lands, because the first crawl of a committee protocol is exactly when some private citizen who testified becomes a "tracked figure".

## Personas: three tiers, and only the first is automatic

**Tier 1 — sitting Knesset members.** This is the right seed and it is almost the only roster in Israeli public life that is *bounded, official, and machine-listable*: 120 people, with official identifiers, party and committee membership as public record. Membership itself is a citable fact, the legal posture for elected officials is the strongest there is, and it maps one-to-one onto the protocol corpus you'd crawl anyway. Within it, prioritise the ~30 who actually generate airtime — ministers, party leaders, committee chairs.

**Tier 2 — officials who aren't MKs.** Ministers from outside the Knesset, ministry spokespeople, agency heads. A handful, added by hand.

**Tier 3 — journalists and commentators.** No authoritative list exists, which means *you* are choosing, which means the choice is the product. I'd hold this tier until the Israeli defamation review lands (the wiki's legal findings are US-only, and the US "public figure" doctrine is doing a lot of work there that Israeli law doesn't necessarily do). When it does open: **write the inclusion rule before the list** — something like "holds a regular paid column or broadcast slot at a national outlet, and comments on public policy" — publish the rule on the methodology page, and let 15–25 names fall out of it. A rule you can defend beats a list you assembled.

## Content: what a statement needs, and who gives it for free

A statement is only citable if it has verbatim text, an unambiguous speaker, an established date, and a stable public URL. Rank candidate sources by how many of those four they hand you:

| Source | The four | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| Knesset plenum & committee protocols | all four | Verbatim, attributed, dated, official, decades deep, no ToS contract. **The backbone, and the "then".** |
| Knesset open data / MK pages | roster, not statements | Where tier 1 comes from |
| gov.il & ministry announcements | mostly | Official and dated, but press-release prose — "the ministry said" is not always "the minister said"; attribution needs care |
| Party feeds & official accounts | mostly | Current and attributed; platform risk if taken through an API |
| Press interviews & op-eds | text and date, ToS-encumbered | Highest value for "now" — and often the only place a position shift is actually *stated* |
| Broadcast | needs ASR | Out of v1 |
| Social platforms | densest "now" | The competitor wiki's sharpest lesson: platform-API dependence is the top cause of death (Politwoops, PolitiTweet). Out of v1 on that evidence. |

**The pairing constraint decides the first pick.** An inconsistency needs two moments about one topic, so two archives of the same era buy you nothing. Start with **protocols (the "then") plus one current official feed (the "now")** covering the same people — that's the minimum combination where analysis has anything to find at all.

## Backfill shape

Don't crawl "everything". The current Knesset plus the previous one is roughly four to six years — far enough back that positions have genuinely moved, and a *finishable* job with a known end. Then the cron feed takes over. The per-source refresh clock already in the registry is built for exactly this asymmetry: a protocol archive and a press feed do not move at the same speed.

## What has to happen first

The recon can't run from here — egress to those hosts is denied by policy, and routing around that isn't on. It needs one sanctioned home: a `workflow_dispatch` job on a GitHub runner that fetches candidate pages and **commits the raw samples**. Everything after that — locating the real data surface, writing the parser, testing it — is offline against those committed bytes, which is also what keeps the parser tests hermetic and network-free.

One design flag while you're deciding: pairing keys on `topics` overlap, and topics currently come from whatever the extractor reads off the source. A protocol gives you a session subject and a press release gives you a title — those won't align. Topic assignment probably needs to be *derived* against a fixed list rather than read from the source, or pairing will silently under-match and the product will look like it found nothing.

**Tier 1 — ~30 high-salience Knesset members.** Ministers, party leaders and committee chairs, not all 120. What waits is publication, not the work.

That ordering has a practical benefit: the **inclusion rule** is the part that needs the review's answer, and writing it against a real candidate list is far easier than writing it in the abstract. Draft the rule and the 15–25 names it selects, review them together, and the review has something concrete to rule on.

The rule is the deliverable, not the list. Roughly: *holds a regular paid column or broadcast slot at a national outlet, and comments on public policy.* It goes on the methodology page, because a rule a reader can check is what separates this from a list somebody assembled.

input.title: Reconnaissance and the first two sources
input.body:
Phase 4 of #25 left the concrete sources to a `map-a-data-source` reconnaissance and the owner's pick. This is that work. The roster it feeds is #31; the two must land together, because the first crawl is when an unrostered speaker first appears.

## The pair to start with, and why it is a pair

An inconsistency needs two moments about one topic, so two archives of the same era buy nothing. The minimum useful combination is one deep historical source and one current one, covering the same people:

1. **Knesset plenum and committee protocols — the "then".** Verbatim, attributed, dated, officially published, decades deep, and no contract to breach. Nothing else in Israeli public life gives all four for free.
2. **One current official feed — the "now".** gov.il and ministry announcements, or party press feeds. Announcement prose needs care on attribution: "the ministry said" is not "the minister said", and only the latter is a statement by a figure.

Deliberately **not** in the first pass: press interviews and op-eds (highest value for a stated position shift, worst on ToS and bot walls — they follow the legal review), broadcast (needs ASR), and social platforms. The last is not a scheduling call: the competitor-landscape wiki's clearest finding is that platform-API dependence is the top cause of death in this space — it killed both politician-tweet archives.

## Backfill window

**The current Knesset plus the previous one** — roughly four to six years. Far enough back that positions have genuinely moved, and a bounded job with an end, rather than an open-ended crawl. Ongoing coverage then runs on the cron, and the per-source `refreshMinutes` already in the registry carries the asymmetry: a protocol archive and a press feed do not move at the same speed.

## Reconnaissance needs a sanctioned home

**It cannot be done from an agent session.** The sandbox's egress policy denies `knesset.gov.il`, `www.gov.il` and `oknesset.org` outright — `403` to CONNECT at the proxy, a policy denial rather than a bot wall — and routing around a policy boundary is not on the table.

So the recon gets one home, which is also the shape the web-scraping rules ask for:

- [ ] A `workflow_dispatch` job on a GitHub runner that fetches a named list of candidate URLs and **commits the raw payloads** as sample fixtures.
- [ ] The `map-a-data-source` recon then runs **offline against those committed bytes**: locate the real data surface in the preferred order — a hydration blob, then a client API, then the markup — and write the findings into a reference doc beside the source module, complete enough that no question about the service needs a second probe.
- [ ] The parser and its per-source case are written against the same committed sample, so the extractor tests need no network and a parser fix costs no requests.
- [ ] Each source module declares its data surface and its refresh clock at registration, which the registry already enforces (`3.7`).

A datacenter IP being blocked is the expected failure here, not a surprise. If a source stays blocked from a runner, the answer is a commercial rendering proxy with the credential in repository secrets — one config-level decision in the fetch module, never a per-scraper workaround.

## Exit

The first two sources each have: a committed real sample, a reference doc, a registered module, and a passing case reading owner-reviewed expected values off the committed bytes. At that point the supported-source matrix becomes spec — each supported source its own leaf — and dropping one becomes a visible change rather than a silent regression.

Blocked on nothing. Needs #31's roster to land alongside it.

Refs #25, #28

input.title: Topics should be derived against a fixed list, not read off the source
input.body:
`analyzeStatement` draws candidate pairs from one figure's statements that share at least one topic (`4.1`), and `topics` currently comes from whatever the extractor read out of the document.

That works for the fixtures because they were written with matching topic strings. It will not work across real sources: a Knesset protocol gives you a session subject, a press release gives you a headline, and an op-ed gives you nothing. Two statements about the same thing will carry different strings, share no topic, never be paired, and never be judged — and the product will look like it simply found nothing. **The failure is silent**: no error, no empty result anyone can see, just a corpus with fewer flags than it should have.

The fix is to make the topic a *derived* property against a fixed vocabulary — classify each statement into zero or more topics from a committed list — rather than a string lifted from the source. Whatever the source called it stays in the raw record; the topic used for pairing is ours and is comparable by construction.

Worth deciding at the same time:

- **Where the vocabulary comes from.** A hand-written list of policy areas is a good start and is reviewable; it also makes the figure page's topic chips mean something consistent.
- **Whether a topic miss should be recoverable.** Pairing on topics is a cost control as much as a correctness rule; if the classifier is unsure, the choice is between paying for a wider pair set and losing the pair. Retaining the classifier's scores makes that tunable later, the same way the surfacing threshold is.
- **What a leaf would assert.** Probably: two statements about the same policy area are paired even when their sources describe them differently — proven over fixtures whose *source* topic strings deliberately disagree, which is exactly what the current fixtures avoid.

Not urgent while the corpus is fixtures. It becomes urgent the moment the second real source lands, because that is when two vocabularies first meet.

Refs #25

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.

- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.

- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

Claudinite loaded, 14 packs, 46 checks, 17,500 rule tokens, 25 available skills, 530 personal preference tokens.

`Comment class: feature`

Straight answer first: **what merged is sized for thousands of statements, not millions.** The extraction contract, raw-before-parse, stable ids, supersede-not-overwrite and the whole test harness carry over unchanged. Three things do not survive the brief you just described, and they're worth naming precisely before I describe the design.

- **Pairing is enumeration.** `candidatePartners` loads every statement a figure has ever made and the analyser judges each one against the new statement. At 30 years that's tens of thousands of rows per message and O(n²) model calls per figure — for one figure with 20k statements, on the order of 200 million judgments. It cannot be scaled, only replaced.
- **There's one store doing two jobs.** D1 holds both everything ever ingested and everything the site serves. A multi-decade corpus and a serving read-model have opposite requirements, and D1 has a per-database ceiling you'd want to check before betting on it either way.
- **The same quote from twenty outlets is twenty statements.** With an extensive source list that's the dominant failure: timelines become twenty copies of one sentence, and the analyser compares a quote to itself.

## The ingestion pipeline

Seven stages, each one a queue hop, each one replayable from the stage before it without a network call:

| Stage | Owns | May not |
|---|---|---|
| **Discover** | enumerate a source's documents in a date window → work items | fetch |
| **Fetch** | one payload → object storage, content-addressed by hash, immutable | interpret |
| **Extract** | payload → *utterances*: speaker-as-written, verbatim text, date, venue metadata | resolve identity |
| **Resolve** | speaker string → persona, with confidence | invent a persona |
| **Normalise** | canonical date, language, topic against a fixed vocabulary, dedupe | drop what it can't classify |
| **Index** | search terms + embeddings | judge |
| **Analyse** | stance, deviation, change points | rewrite history |

The rule that makes the whole thing survivable: **every stage is a pure function of the stage before it plus committed inputs.** A parser fix, a better resolver, a new topic vocabulary — each replays from storage over the whole corpus, costs zero requests, and produces the same ids it produced last time.

## The two model changes that do the real work

**1. Utterance and attestation, not statement.** One thing said once is an *utterance*. Every place we saw it is an *attestation*, each with its own outlet, publication date, and URL. This kills the duplicate problem, and it's also exactly the structure your anomaly question needs: it makes "he said this, and here is the venue" a first-class fact rather than something inferred from which scraper happened to find it. So **venue and audience become fields on the record** — the setting (plenary, interview, rally, party forum, op-ed) and who was being addressed (national broadcast, party members, foreign press). An anomaly whose interest is *who he was talking to* is unanswerable unless that's modelled at ingestion; it can't be recovered later.

**2. Positions, not pairs.** You described two different things, and they want two different mechanisms:

- A **position** is (persona, topic, stance, time window), derived from many utterances. A figure's stance on a topic becomes a series over time.
- A **trend change** is a change point in that series. What you want from it — *when* it happened — is exactly what a change point is. The "why" stays out of the automated claim; the honest output is the date and the utterances on either side of it.
- An **anomaly** is a single utterance that deviates from the prevailing position *at the time it was said*. That's a one-against-one comparison, not one-against-all — and the deviation is only interesting alongside its venue, which is why the two changes are really one change.

This also solves the scale problem as a side effect: each new utterance is compared to the figure's current position on its topic, not to every prior utterance. Cost goes from O(n²) to O(n), and retrieval (embeddings over the topic's utterances) supplies the handful of comparisons a model actually needs to see.

## Storage: a ledger and a read model

- **R2, raw** — payloads, content-addressed, immutable, never re-fetched.
- **R2, ledger** — the extracted utterance record, partitioned by source and date. The durable master, and the thing every replay reads. Unbounded and cheap, and it's the committed-raw-record discipline scaled past what a git tree can hold.
- **D1, serving** — only what the site shows: the roster, published utterances, positions, live flags. Bounded by the product rather than by history, which is the only way it stays a sensible size.

## Backfill is a second lane, not a bigger cron

Discovery over a 30-year window is a resumable bulk job with a beginning and an end; the hourly feed is a small idempotent tail. Same extraction code, different driver. The bulk lane needs durable execution and parallelism that a cron-triggered Worker does not have — and it needs to be safe to kill and restart, because it will be.

Two flags on the far end of that window: the further back you go the more a "source" is a **scan rather than HTML**, so extraction needs OCR with a confidence that travels with the text; and **names move** over 30 years — rank, role, marriage, spelling. The roster's name forms have to be time-scoped, or resolution silently splits one person into three.

## Where the privacy rule lives

Not in a filter at the end — in the shape of the pipeline. **We index documents; we build person-records only for people on the roster.** A committee protocol is public record and belongs in the ledger whole. But an utterance whose speaker doesn't resolve to a roster persona is never indexed against a person, never published, and never judged. [#31](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/31) is that gate; this makes it structural rather than a policy someone has to remember.

These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. ## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

# hitbut — service architecture The end state of hitbut's runtime: what runs where, what it stores, and how a public statement travels from a source on the web to a browsable inconsistency with evidence attached. The deployment boundary itself — Workers back end, Pages front end, `src/shared` as the only shared surface — is [`src/README.md`](../../src/README.md)'s; this document describes what runs inside that boundary, and why this shape over the alternatives. ## The system at a glance ```mermaid flowchart LR S[Public sources
transcripts, press releases,
official feeds, archives] subgraph W [backend — one Cloudflare Worker] A[acquisition
cron-triggered scrapers] C[(corpus
D1 + R2)] N[analysis
queue consumer] P[HTTP API
/api/v1] end F[frontend — Cloudflare Pages
static site] S --> A --> C C --> N --> C C --> P --> F ``` ## One Worker, three responsibilities The back end deploys as a **single Worker** with three entry points: a cron trigger runs acquisition, a queue consumer runs analysis, and the fetch handler serves the API. The three responsibilities stay separable as modules (`src/backend/acquisition/`, `analysis/`, `api/`), with `src/backend/corpus/` the only module the other three import — no acquisition code in the API path, no API code in a scraper. *Alternative — three Workers behind service bindings*: rejected for now. It buys process isolation the product doesn't need yet and costs three deploys, three configs, and RPC across what is currently one data model. The module boundaries keep that split cheap if scale ever demands it. .... 10:## The system at a glance 27:## One Worker, three responsibilities 41:## Storage 63:## Data model and stable identifiers 81:## Acquisition 96:## Analysis 110:## HTTP API 119:## Frontend 130:## How requirements are proven against this

cat > docs/architecture/DESIGN.md <<'DESIGNEOF' # hitbut — service architecture The end state of hitbut's runtime: what runs where, what it stores, and how a public statement travels from a source on the web to a browsable inconsistency with evidence attached. The deployment boundary itself — Workers back end, Pages front end, `src/shared` as the only shared surface — is [`src/README.md`](../../src/README.md)'s; this document describes what runs inside that boundary, and why this shape over the alternatives. Two words for one thing: the product says **persona**, the code and the API say **figure**. They are the same entity, and the code keeps its word because a rename across a shipped schema, spec and site buys vocabulary and costs citations. ## The system at a glance ```mermaid flowchart LR S[Public sources
transcripts, archives,
official feeds, press] subgraph W [backend — one Cloudflare Worker + one Workflow] B[backfill
Workflow, one run per slice] A[acquisition
cron, the moving edge] I[ingestion
resolve · merge · embed] C[(corpus
D1 + R2 + Vectorize)] N[analysis
stance series] P[HTTP API
/api/v1] end F[frontend — Cloudflare Pages
static site] S --> B --> I S --> A --> I I --> C C --> N --> C C --> P --> F ``` ## One Worker, four responsibilities, plus a Workflow The back end deploys as a **single Worker**: a cron trigger runs acquisition over the moving edge, queue consumers run ingestion and analysis, and the fetch handler serves the API. Each stays a separate module — `acquisition/`, `ingestion/`, `analysis/`, `api/` — over the one module they all import, `corpus/`. The **historical backfill is a Workflow**, not a cron: it is a job with an end, measured in days, over decades of archives, and it needs durable execution with per-step retry rather than a schedule. It shares the Worker's bindings and its ingestion code; what differs is only how it is driven. *Alternative — a long-running job off-platform, writing to R2*: rejected in favour of keeping one runtime and one deployment target. The bet is that the backfill decomposes into slices that each fit inside a Workflow's limits. **That bet is unverified** — Cloudflare's published step, duration and payload limits could not be read while this was written, and no number here should be trusted until someone checks them against the docs. If a slice does not fit, the escape hatch is a smaller slice before it is a second runtime. ## Storage - **D1** holds the ledger everything reads: personas, utterances, attestations, cluster assignments, stances, findings, and the full-text index for search. Relational queries — a persona's timeline, a stance series, an attestation's siblings — are the workload. - **R2** holds the raw payload cache: every fetched page, feed response or document is stored verbatim, keyed by source and fetch time, **before** anything interprets it. A parser fix then re-runs extraction offline against R2 — no re-fetch, no dependence on sites that changed or died. R2 also holds the backfill's intermediate ledger and the generated NDJSON export snapshots. - **Vectorize** holds one embedding per utterance. D1 has no vector type, and the retrieval this product needs is nearest-neighbour, not `LIKE`. - **Queues** carry the hand-off between stages, so a fetch burst never waits on model latency and a failed stage retries without re-fetching. *Alternatives*: KV rejected — no queries, and the corpus is nothing but queries. Durable Objects rejected — no per-entity coordination exists that D1 row writes don't already serialize. Committing extracted raw records to git (the web-scraping pack's default) is adapted rather than adopted: decades of archives outgrow a git tree, so R2 is the durable raw store, and only the committed per-source *sample* payloads used as test fixtures live in the repo. ## Data model and stable identifiers Stable identifiers are a product requirement — researchers and journalists cite them — so **no identifier is ever reused, renumbered, or deleted**; retirement is a status, not a deletion. - **persona (`figure`)** — slug id, display name, role, aliases, status. The roster is a **committed input**, not a byproduct of crawling: a speaker who is not on it never becomes a tracked persona. Personas are people who put themselves in the public eye, in the capacity in which they did so. - **utterance** — ULID. One thing said once: the persona, the normalized text, when it was said, and the language. This is the unit analysis reasons over. - **attestation** — ULID. One document reporting an utterance: the source, its URL, the text *as that document renders it*, the venue it was said in, the audience it was addressed to, when the document was published, and the R2 key of the raw payload. **Many attestations per utterance** — one speech carried by five outlets is one utterance and five attestations, not five statements. Without the split, a persona is compared against themselves and every echo reads as agreement. - **date precision** — `said_at` carries a precision (`day`, `month`, `year`) beside it. Thirty years back, a source often establishes "March 1998" and no more; recording that as the first of the month invents a fact, and recording it as unknown discards one. A date the source does not establish at all stays null — never defaulted. - **cluster** — an emergent subject, discovered from the corpus rather than chosen in advance (§ Analysis). Ids are stable; the human-readable label is regenerated and is display only. - **stance** — one utterance's position within one cluster, with the model and prompt version that produced it. - **finding** — ULID. A surfaced inconsistency: its kind (`anomaly` or `trend-change`), the utterances it rests on, its rationale, its score, and the model and prompt versions. Re-analysis writes a new finding and marks the old one superseded, so a cited finding stays resolvable forever. ## Acquisition and backfill Per-source modules behind **one shared fetch module** — retries, backoff, bot-wall detection, and raw-before-parse discipline live there once. Each source module declares the data surface it reads (hydration blob, client API, or markup — in that order of preference), its own refresh clock, and an extractor from raw payload to candidate utterances. Fields the extractor doesn't yet understand are preserved in the raw record, not dropped. Two drivers over the same modules: - **The backfill** walks a source's archive in slices — a year of one archive is the working unit — as one Workflow run per slice. A slice that fails retries without touching its neighbours, and the window is finite, so the job has an end. - **The cron** covers the moving edge, on each source's own clock. A transcript archive and a press feed do not move at the same speed, and running everything on the fastest one re-learns a static document thousands of times. Cloudflare egress comes from datacenter IPs, which some sources bot-block; if a source needs it, the fetch module routes through a commercial rendering proxy — a config-level credential, not a per-scraper decision. **Scanned archives are the open risk.** Material from the 1990s is often a scan behind a PDF, which means OCR, which is the one stage with no obvious home inside a Worker. It may force that stage — and only that stage — somewhere else. ## Ingestion Everything between "bytes arrived" and "the corpus changed". It is one pipeline whichever driver fed it, and **every stage is idempotent**, because both drivers retry: Workflows retries a step, the queue redelivers a message. 1. **Fetch** — raw payload to R2 before any parse, addressed by content hash. An unchanged hash means extraction is skipped entirely on a re-run. 2. **Extract** — the source module turns a payload into candidate utterances, each carrying the document's own venue and audience metadata. 3. **Resolve** — the speaker string becomes a roster persona, through aliases and the document's own context. A speaker who is not on the roster is **retained unattributed**, never promoted and never dropped: the raw record stays complete and a person decides later. 4. **Merge** — a candidate becomes either a new utterance or another attestation of an existing one. Identity is the persona, the date, and near-identity of the text; the same speech quoted at three lengths is one utterance whose longest attestation is the fullest record of it. 5. **Embed** — one vector per utterance into Vectorize. 6. **Assign** — the utterance joins the nearest existing cluster, or opens a new one when nothing is near enough. 7. **Stance** — one model call places the utterance on its cluster's own axis. Steps 5–7 are what make the corpus queryable by *position* rather than only by word, and each is O(1) per utterance. ## Analysis The product's claim is that a persona's record is checkable, so detection has to be defensible before it is clever: for every finding, a reader can see which utterances it rests on, what was said about them, and by which model and prompt. **Subjects are discovered, not declared.** There is no committed list of topics. Utterances are embedded, and clusters emerge from where they fall; a label is generated for a cluster afterwards and is shown to readers, but pairing and detection key on the cluster id, never the label. A vocabulary chosen in advance would decide in advance what the corpus is allowed to be about, and two sources describing one subject differently would never meet. **Embedding distance measures aboutness, not agreement.** "I will not cut a shekel from this line" and "this line was never a priority of mine" sit close together in embedding space — they are about the same thing, which is exactly why they are worth comparing and exactly why distance alone cannot tell you they conflict. So the embedding does retrieval, and a second, cheap step does judgment: for each utterance, one model call places it on the axis its cluster already implies, and that value is stored with its confidence and its model and prompt version. What that buys is a **stance series**: for each persona and each cluster, a sequence of positions through time. Two kinds of finding fall out of it: - **Anomaly** — an utterance that deviates from the persona's prevailing stance in that cluster *at that date*. The interesting attribute is then **who they were talking to**: the venue and the audience, which the attestation carries precisely so this question is answerable. - **Trend change** — a change point in the series. The interesting attribute is **when** it happened, and the finding reports the interval the change falls in. *Why* it happened is out of scope; a bounded, sourced "between these two dates, this position moved" is the claim the corpus can actually support. *Alternative — judge every pair of statements*: rejected. It is O(n²) model calls against a corpus meant to hold decades, it needs a topic vocabulary to keep the pair count survivable, and a trend is invisible to it — no two statements are where a trend lives. The pairwise page survives as a *view*: the two most representative utterances either side of a change point are what the inconsistency page shows. Only findings above a surfacing threshold reach the product; the full distribution is kept for tuning. The model call sits behind one interface, so moving to a different model or an external provider is a config change rather than a rewrite. ## HTTP API Read-only public JSON under a versioned path (`/api/v1/...`): personas, a persona's timeline, utterance detail with its attestations, findings, and search. Cursor pagination, open CORS, no accounts, no write surface — the only writers are the cron trigger, the Workflow and the queue consumers. Responses are edge-cacheable with short TTLs; bulk export is served as generated snapshots from R2 rather than paginated through D1. ## Frontend A static site on Cloudflare Pages — no Pages Functions, no server rendering: everything the site shows is public and comes from `/api/v1`, so the API stays the one back end and the front end stays a pile of cacheable assets. Page inventory: home (search + recent findings), persona (profile, timeline, findings), utterance detail (text, attestations, sources), finding detail (the utterances side by side with rationale and sources), search results, and a methodology page explaining how detection works and how to report an error. ## How requirements are proven against this Data-level requirements (extraction, corpus invariants, ingestion, analysis) assert on values directly, with committed real sample payloads as fixtures, and with the model and the vector store behind interfaces a case can script. UI requirements drive this front end in headless Chromium against a local `wrangler` preview of the real deployment, asserting on committed screenshot goldens — the harness runs what ships, not a mock shell. input.body:
The tracking issue for the redesign in [`docs/architecture/DESIGN.md`](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/blob/main/docs/architecture/DESIGN.md) (PR pending). The design doc carries the end state and the rationale; this issue carries only the phases and their exit conditions. Append-only once agreed.

**What changed and why.** v1 (#25) shipped a corpus of flat statements judged in pairs against a topic list read off the source. Three things break that at the scale now intended — decades of archives, many sources, a big roster: one speech carried by five outlets became five statements; pairwise judging is O(n²) and cannot see a trend at all; and a topic vocabulary decides in advance what the corpus may be about. The replacement is utterances with many attestations, subjects discovered by embedding, and a stance series per persona per subject.

**This is cheap now and expensive later.** The corpus is fixtures, so this is a rewrite of code and spec, not a migration of cited data. After the first real source it becomes the hard case the stable-id promise exists to prevent.

## Phases

**0. Provisioning (human-only, front-loaded)** — see the comment added to #27
- [ ] Vectorize index created and bound; Workflows enabled on the account.
- [ ] The embedding model and the stance model chosen, both reachable from the Worker.
- [ ] Exit: `wrangler deploy --dry-run` resolves the new bindings from the committed config.

**1. Verify the Workflow bet**
- [ ] Read Cloudflare's published step, duration and payload limits for Workflows and check a one-year archive slice against them. **They could not be read from the session that wrote the design** — the doc says so rather than asserting numbers.
- [ ] Exit: either a slice size that provably fits, or a recorded decision to slice smaller / move the stage.

**2. Spec first**
- [ ] Rewrite the affected leaves in `dev/requirements/requirements.md`: utterance vs attestation, date precision, roster resolution (#31), emergent clusters, stance, the two finding kinds. Watch the coverage gate go red before any case exists.
- [ ] Exit: the gate is red for exactly the new leaves, green once claimed.

**3. Data model**
- [ ] `utterances` + `attestations` replace `statements`; `said_at_precision`; `clusters`, `stances`, `findings`.
- [ ] Exit: logic cases prove one speech across three documents is one utterance and three attestations; that a month-precision date is neither a day nor unknown; that supersede-not-overwrite still holds for findings.

**4. Ingestion**
- [ ] The pipeline as one module — fetch, extract, resolve, merge, embed, assign, stance — every stage idempotent under retry.
- [ ] Exit: behavior cases prove a replayed payload writes nothing new, an unrostered speaker is retained unattributed, and the same quote at three lengths merges to one utterance.

**5. Embedding, clustering, stance**
- [ ] Vector store and stance model behind interfaces a case can script; online cluster assignment; stance stored with model and prompt version.
- [ ] Exit: cases over fixtures where the *source* topic strings deliberately disagree still cluster together (#33), and a scripted stance model produces a readable series.

**6. Detection**
- [ ] Anomaly (deviation from prevailing stance, carrying venue and audience) and trend change (change point, reported as an interval).
- [ ] Exit: cases over a synthetic series with a planted step change and a planted outlier find each, and find nothing in a flat series.

**7. Backfill Workflow**
- [ ] One run per archive slice, sharing the ingestion code, resumable per step.
- [ ] Exit: a slice runs end to end against fixtures; a deliberately failed step retries without re-fetching.

**8. API and site**
- [ ] `/api/v1` and the six pages carry utterances, attestations and findings. The inconsistency page keeps its shape: the two representative utterances either side of a change point.
- [ ] Exit: server and screen lanes green; goldens refreshed and reviewed.

Ordering: 0 and 1 front-loaded → 2 → 3 → 4 → {5, 6} → 7 → 8. Review lands as one stack, not a wait per phase.

## Out of scope

*Why* a trend changed — the design settles for when. Cross-persona comparison. Anything that would need a source we have not agreed to take.

Refs #25, #31, #32, #33

input.title: Redesign ingestion and analysis around utterances and stance series
input.body:
Documentation only — `docs/architecture/DESIGN.md`. It replaces the ingestion and analysis architecture v1 shipped, for a corpus meant to hold decades of statements from a large roster. The implementation plan is #34.

## What changes, and what forced each change

**One speech, five outlets, five "statements".** v1 stored a flat statement per extraction. Across many sources that turns every echo of one speech into a separate record, so a persona gets compared against themselves and agreement is manufactured. The corpus becomes **utterances** (the thing said once) with **many attestations** (each document reporting it). Venue and audience live on the attestation, which is what makes "who were they talking to?" answerable at all.

**Thirty years back, a date is often a month.** `said_at` gains a precision. Recording "March 1998" as the first of the month invents a fact; recording it as unknown discards one. Same principle the corpus already applies to unknown dates, extended to partial ones.

**Subjects are discovered, not declared.** No committed topic list. Utterances are embedded, clusters emerge, and labels are generated afterwards for display only — pairing keys on the cluster id. A vocabulary chosen in advance decides in advance what the corpus is allowed to be about, and two sources describing one subject differently never meet (#33).

**Embedding distance measures aboutness, not agreement** — this is the load-bearing caveat. *"I will not cut a shekel from this line"* and *"this line was never a priority of mine"* sit close together: same subject, opposite position. That closeness is exactly why they are worth comparing and exactly why distance alone cannot judge them. So retrieval is the embedding's job, and a second cheap call places each utterance on its cluster's own axis.

**That gives a stance series**, and the two findings the owner asked for fall out of it: an **anomaly** is a deviation from the prevailing stance at that date (venue and audience are the interesting part), a **trend change** is a change point (the date is). Pairwise judging is dropped: O(n²) model calls, dependent on a topic vocabulary to stay survivable, and blind to trends — no two statements are where a trend lives. The inconsistency page survives unchanged as a *view* onto a change point.

**The backfill becomes a Workflow**, one run per archive slice, sharing the Worker's ingestion code — a job with an end and per-step retry, rather than a schedule.

## One thing deliberately not asserted

Cloudflare's docs are unreachable from this environment, so the Workflow step, duration and payload limits are **unverified**. The doc says so in the text rather than quoting numbers from memory, and checking them is phase 1 of #34 — before any code bets on the slice size.

Scanned 1990s archives needing OCR are flagged as the one stage with no obvious home inside a Worker.

## Folders touched

```
docs/architecture/   DESIGN.md — the diagram, storage (Vectorize added), the data
                     model (utterance/attestation/date precision/cluster/stance/
                     finding), acquisition split into backfill and moving edge, a
                     new ingestion section, and analysis rewritten around
                     emergent clusters and stance series
```

No code changes; the suite is untouched and green.

Refs #25, #31, #32, #33
Closes #34 — no: #34 is the implementation plan and stays open.
