content.text: {"id":"4335837762","url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/pull/35"}

Your instinct is right, and there's one caveat that ends up shaping the whole pipeline.

**Yes to embeddings — but distance measures *aboutness*, not agreement.** "I will not cut a shekel from this line" and "this line was never a priority of mine" sit very close together in embedding space. Same subject, opposite position. That closeness is exactly why the two are worth comparing, and exactly why distance alone can't tell you they conflict — a pure nearest-neighbour system would rank a persona's most emphatic agreement and their flattest contradiction as equally similar.

So the embedding does the job it's genuinely good at, and a second step does the judging:

- **Embedding → retrieval.** It replaces the topic join entirely, which is what you wanted: no pre-created list. Clusters emerge from where utterances actually fall, and a human-readable label gets generated for a cluster *afterwards*, for display only. Pairing keys on the cluster id, never the label — so two sources describing one subject in different words still meet.
- **One cheap call → stance.** Per utterance, place it on the axis its cluster already implies, and store the value with its confidence and the model and prompt version.

That's O(n) embeddings plus O(n) stance calls, against O(n²) for pairwise judging — and it's not just cheaper, it can see something pairwise can't.

**What it buys is a stance series**: for each persona, in each subject, a sequence of positions through time. Your two cases fall straight out of it. An **anomaly** is an utterance that deviates from the prevailing stance *at that date* — and then the interesting attribute is who they were addressing, which is why venue and audience have to live on the record. A **trend change** is a change point in the series, reported as the interval it falls in. I've scoped *why* it changed out, per your "we'll be happy with when".

**The ingestion pipeline** is seven stages, one path whichever driver fed it, every stage idempotent because both drivers retry: fetch (raw to R2 before any parse, addressed by content hash, so an unchanged hash skips extraction) → extract → resolve the speaker against the roster → merge into utterances and attestations → embed → assign to a cluster → stance.

The merge step is where your approved split pays off: one speech carried by five outlets becomes **one utterance and five attestations**, not five statements. Without it a persona is compared against themselves and every echo reads as agreement. And I added something you didn't ask for but 20–30 years forces: `said_at` carries a **precision**. A 1998 source often establishes "March" and no more — writing that as the 1st invents a fact, writing it as unknown throws one away.

Your definition of who's trackable is now the design's, verbatim in intent: personas are people who put themselves in the public eye, in the capacity in which they did so. That's the roster rule in [#31](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/31).

```
docs/architecture/   DESIGN.md — new diagram; Vectorize added to storage; the
                     data model rebuilt around utterance/attestation, date
                     precision, clusters, stances and findings; acquisition
                     split into a backfill Workflow and the moving-edge cron;
                     a new ingestion section; analysis rewritten around
                     emergent clusters and stance series
```

Two things I'd flag rather than let you discover later. **Workflows is your call and I've taken it, but I couldn't verify it** — Cloudflare's docs are blocked from this sandbox, so the design says the slice-fits-in-a-Workflow bet is unverified instead of quoting limits from memory; checking it is phase 1 of the plan, before any code depends on the slice size. And **scanned archives**: 1990s material is often a PDF scan, which means OCR, which is the one stage with no obvious home inside a Worker — it may force that single stage somewhere else.

[PR #35](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/pull/35) is the design doc; [#34](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/34) is the implementation plan, spec-first with the coverage gate going red before any case exists. I've also added the Vectorize index and Workflows to the provisioning checklist in [#27](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/27), with a note that the embedding model and the stance model are different shapes and may not come from the same provider.

> ⚠️ Still open: [#35](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/pull/35) awaits your review — it rewrites the analysis architecture that merged this morning, so it's worth reading before it lands; the Workflows limits check is phase 1 of [#34](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/34) and blocks committing to a slice size; OCR for scanned archives has no home yet; and the earlier items stand — provisioning ([#27](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/27)), the recon green-light ([#32](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/32)), the legal review ([#28](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/28)), and the environment setup script re-paste.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

=== deploy job ===
  deploy:
    name: ship main
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    needs: [checks, screen]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
      CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
      - name: Is there an account to deploy to yet?
        id: account
        run: |
          if [ -z "$CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" ] || [ -z "$CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID" ]; then
            echo "Cloudflare provisioning (issue #27) has not landed — nothing to deploy yet."
            echo "ready=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "ready=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
      - if: steps.account.outputs.ready == 'true'
        run: npm ci
      - name: Bring the corpus schema up to date
        if: steps.account.outputs.ready == 'true'
        run: npm run corpus:migrate:remote
      - name: Deploy the Worker
        if: steps.account.outputs.ready == 'true'
        run: npm run deploy:api
      - name: Build the site against the deployed API
        if: steps.account.outputs.ready == 'true'
        env:
          VITE_API_ORIGIN: ${{ vars.API_ORIGIN }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$VITE_API_ORIGIN" ]; then
            echo "::error::the API_ORIGIN repository variable is unset — the site would ship pointing at itself"
            exit 1
          fi
          npm run build:site
      - name: Deploy the site
        if: steps.account.outputs.ready == 'true'
        run: npm run deploy:site

{"number":35,"title":"Redesign ingestion and analysis around utterances and stance series","body":"Documentation only — `docs/architecture/DESIGN.md`. It replaces the ingestion and analysis architecture v1 shipped, for a corpus meant to hold decades of statements from a large roster. The implementation plan is #34, which stays open after this merges.

## What changes, and what forced each change

**One speech, five outlets, five "statements".** v1 stored a flat statement per extraction. Across many sources that turns every echo of one speech into a separate record, so a persona gets compared against themselves and agreement is manufactured. The corpus becomes **utterances** (the thing said once) with **many attestations** (each document reporting it). Venue and audience live on the attestation, which is what makes "who were they talking to?" answerable at all.

**Thirty years back, a date is often a month.** `said_at` gains a precision. Recording "March 1998" as the first of the month invents a fact; recording it as unknown discards one. Same principle the corpus already applies to unknown dates, extended to partial ones.

**Subjects are discovered, not declared.** No committed topic list. Utterances are embedded, clusters emerge, and labels are generated afterwards for display only — pairing keys on the cluster id. A vocabulary chosen in advance decides in advance what the corpus is allowed to be about, and two sources describing one subject differently never meet (#33).

**Embedding distance measures aboutness, not agreement** — this is the load-bearing caveat. *"I will not cut a shekel from this line"* and *"this line was never a priority of mine"* sit close together: same subject, opposite position. That closeness is exactly why they are worth comparing and exactly why distance alone cannot judge them. So retrieval is the embedding's job, and a second cheap call places each utterance on its cluster's own axis.

**That gives a stance series**, and the two findings the owner asked for fall out of it: an **anomaly** is a deviation from the prevailing stance at that date (venue and audience are the interesting part), a **trend change** is a change point (the date is). Pairwise judging is dropped: O(n²) model calls, dependent on a topic vocabulary to stay survivable, and blind to trends — no two statements are where a trend lives. The inconsistency page survives unchanged as a *view* onto a change point.

**The backfill becomes a Workflow**, one run per archive slice, sharing the Worker's ingestion code — a job with an end and per-step retry, rather than a schedule.

## One thing deliberately not asserted

Cloudflare's docs are unreachable from this environment, so the Workflow step, duration and payload limits are **unverified**. The doc says so in the text rather than quoting numbers from memory, and checking them is phase 1 of #34 — before any code bets on the slice size.

Scanned 1990s archives needing OCR are flagged as the one stage with no obvious home inside a Worker.

## Folders touched

```
docs/architecture/   DESIGN.md — the diagram, storage (Vectorize added), the data
                     model (utterance/attestation/date precision/cluster/stance/
                     finding), acquisition split into backfill and moving edge, a
                     new ingestion section, and analysis rewritten around
                     emergent clusters and stance series
```

No code changes; the suite is untouched and green.

Refs #25, #31, #32, #33, #34

PR [#35](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/pull/35) is still open and mergeable, so what's below describes `main` as it stands today.

Reading the deploy job end to end, there are two ordering traps in it that are worth naming before the checklist, because you'd otherwise hit them at 11pm.

input.body:
Phase 0 of #25. Every step here needs the Cloudflare dashboard or the repo's secret store, so none of it can be done from a session — this is the checklist for whoever has those. The code that consumes each resource is written and its binding name is already fixed in `wrangler.toml`. Local development and the whole test suite run against wrangler's local D1/R2/Queues and need none of this: **what is blocked is production only.** **Consolidated 2026-08-22** — this body now holds every step, in the order they have to happen. It previously carried a flat list plus two comments; nothing has been dropped, but the ordering below is load-bearing and the flat list hid it. --- ## A. Only a human can do these - [ ] **Pick the Cloudflare account**, and copy its Account ID. - [ ] **Create a scoped API token** with *Workers Scripts:Edit, D1:Edit, R2:Edit, Queues:Edit, Pages:Edit, Vectorize:Edit, Workers AI:Read*. - [ ] **Paste both as repository secrets**: `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` and `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → *Secrets*).
*While off:* the deploy job detects the missing credentials, says so, and exits clean. Nothing else in this list can be done either, because everything below needs the token. ## B. Create the resources Each one exists before the first deploy, because `wrangler deploy` fails when a binding names a resource that is not there — it does not create them for you. - [ ] **D1 database** `hitbut-corpus`.
*While off:* the Worker has no corpus; every API route 500s. - [ ] **R2 bucket** `hitbut-raw` (binding `RAW`).
*While off:* no raw-payload cache and no bulk NDJSON export; a parser fix would need a re-fetch. - [ ] **Queue** `hitbut-analysis` (producer + consumer, both already in `wrangler.toml`).
*While off:* acquisition cannot hand statements to analysis; nothing gets judged. - [ ] **Enable Workers AI** on the account (binding `AI`).
*While off:* analysis has no judge; pairs are drawn and never scored. - [ ] **Vectorize index** for utterance embeddings, bound as `VECTORS` (from #34). Its dimension count is fixed at creation and must match the chosen embedding model — **pick the model first**.
*While off:* nothing can be clustered or compared by position; detection has no retrieval step and finds nothing. - [ ] **Enable Workflows** on the account (from #34).
*While off:* the historical backfill has no runtime. The moving-edge cron still works, so the site would carry only what was said after launch — which is the half of the product that is not the point. - [ ] **Pages project** named `hitbut`, no build command (CI uploads the built `dist/`). Create it explicitly rather than relying on the CLI to create it — a non-interactive runner cannot answer a prompt.
*While off:* there is no site. Note on models: the redesign needs **two** model calls of different shapes — an embedding model (one vector per utterance, high volume, cheap) and a stance model (one judgment per utterance, low volume, needs real Hebrew competence). They may not come from the same provider, and #28's item 3 — Hebrew competence unevaluated — applies to the second. ## C. One step lands as a commit, not a click - [ ] **Paste the real `database_id`** into the `[[d1_databases]]` block in `wrangler.toml`, replacing the all-zeros placeholder, and merge it.
*While off:* the migrate step runs against a database id that does not exist and the deploy fails on its first real step. ## D. The first deploy takes two passes, by design The site is static, so the API's origin is baked in at build time — and that origin does not exist until the Worker has been deployed once. So: - [ ] **Let the deploy run** (merging C is enough). It applies the migrations and ships the Worker; the site build then fails, on purpose, with *"the API_ORIGIN repository variable is unset"*. - [ ] **Copy the deployed Worker's origin** (`https://hitbut-api..workers.dev`, or the custom domain if you put one in front of it) into the repository **variable** `API_ORIGIN` — Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → *Variables*, not Secrets. - [ ] **Re-run the `product` workflow** on `main` (Actions → product → Run workflow — `workflow_dispatch` is wired and the deploy job accepts it). This pass builds the site against the real origin and ships it. Every deploy after this one is a single pass with no human step, which is requirement `7.1`. **Closes when** the `product` workflow on `main` is green end to end — its dry-run job passes against the committed `wrangler.toml`, and one merge is observed reaching the deployed site with no human build step. #30 checks for exactly that and reports back on its own. Refs #25, #34 --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

input.title: The deploy has no smoke test and no rollback path
input.body:
The `ship main` job in `.github/workflows/product.yml` applies migrations, deploys the Worker, builds the site and deploys Pages. Then it stops. Nothing checks that the thing it just shipped answers.

Two consequences:

**A deploy that passed CI can still be broken in production.** Everything the suite proves is proven against a local `workerd` with local D1, R2 and Queues (#28, item 1). A missing binding, an unapplied migration, a wrong `API_ORIGIN`, a Pages project pointing at the wrong output — every one of those is invisible to CI and fatal in production, and today the job goes green for all of them.

**There is no way back.** No step captures what was previously deployed, and nothing in the repo describes how to return to it. When the site is wrong at 2am the question "what do I do right now" has no answer written down.

## What to add

input.title: Schema changes need expand/contract once the corpus holds data
input.body:
The deploy job applies migrations **before** it deploys the Worker:

```
Bring the corpus schema up to date   →   Deploy the Worker
```

That order is correct for an additive migration and wrong for any other kind. Between those two steps the *old* Worker is still serving against the *new* schema. Add a column and nothing notices. Rename or drop one, and every request in that window hits a schema its code does not know.

Right now this is harmless — the corpus is empty and there is no traffic. It stops being harmless twice over:

1. **When the site is live**, that window is real user-facing errors.
2. **When #34 lands**, the change is exactly the dangerous kind: `statements` becomes `utterances` plus `attestations`, and columns move. A single migration that renames in place would break the running Worker for the length of a deploy.

## What this needs

The standard three-step discipline, made explicit in the repo so a migration author cannot skip it by accident:

- **Expand** — add the new tables and columns; deploy code that writes both shapes and reads the old one.
- **Migrate** — backfill the new shape; deploy code that reads the new one.
- **Contract** — drop the old shape, in a later deploy, once nothing reads it.

Each step is its own merge, and the middle one cannot be skipped just because the corpus is small at the time. Worth a check that fails a migration file containing `DROP`, `RENAME` or a `NOT NULL` addition unless it is marked as the contract step of a named expand — the same shape as the other repo checks, so the rule is enforced rather than remembered.

Filed while answering how deployments work; not urgent until the corpus has data or #34 starts.

content.text: {"id":"5219124018","url":"https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/37"}

Here's the whole picture.

## The steady state, once it's set up

A merge to `main` is the entire deploy trigger. The `product` workflow runs three jobs: the fast lanes plus a `wrangler` dry-run, the screen lane in the pinned browser container, and then — only if both pass — `ship main`, which applies the D1 migrations, deploys the Worker, builds the site against the deployed API, and deploys Pages. **No human step**, which is requirement `7.1`, and [#30](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/30) is the mechanism that comes back to confirm it actually happened.

Until the account exists, that last job detects the missing credentials, says so, and exits clean — an unprovisioned account is an expected state, not a broken build.

## Two traps in the first deploy

**The first deploy cannot succeed in one pass, by design.** The site is static, so the API's origin is compiled into the bundle — and that origin doesn't exist until the Worker has been deployed once. So the first run ships the Worker and then deliberately fails the site build with *"the API_ORIGIN repository variable is unset"*. You copy the Worker's URL into the `API_ORIGIN` variable, re-run the workflow (`workflow_dispatch` is wired and the deploy job accepts it), and the second pass ships the site. Every deploy after that is one pass.

**`wrangler deploy` does not create the resources its bindings name — it fails.** The D1 database, R2 bucket, queue, Vectorize index and Pages project all have to exist first. That's why the checklist is ordered rather than a flat list.

## What actually needs a human

I've rewritten [#27](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/27) into one ordered checklist — it had drifted across a body and two comments, and the ordering is the part that matters. Four groups:

**A. Genuinely human-only** — pick the account and copy its ID, create a scoped API token, paste both as repo secrets. That's it; everything else is downstream of the token.

**B. Create the resources** — D1, R2, the queue, Workers AI, the Vectorize index, Workflows, the Pages project. Dashboard clicks, one time. Note the Vectorize index has its dimension fixed at creation, so the embedding model gets chosen *before* it.

**C. One step is a commit, not a click** — the real `database_id` replaces the all-zeros placeholder in `wrangler.toml` and merges. Easy to miss on a checklist that reads like dashboard work.

**D. The two-pass first deploy** described above.

## Two gaps I found reading the job

**[#36](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/36) — nothing checks that the deploy worked, and there's no way back.** Everything the suite proves is proven against a *local* workerd. A missing binding, an unapplied migration, a wrong `API_ORIGIN` — all invisible to CI, all fatal in production, and today the job goes green for every one of them. There's also no rollback written down, which means the 2am question has no answer.

**[#37](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/37) — migrations run before the Worker deploys**, which is correct for additive changes and wrong for any other kind: in that window the old Worker serves against the new schema. Harmless now with an empty corpus; not harmless when [#34](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/34) turns `statements` into `utterances` and `attestations`.

Under #34 the deploy also grows a Workflow deployment and the `VECTORS` binding — and note the backfill itself is **not** part of the deploy. It's a job you start deliberately, not something a merge kicks off.

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. - **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

import pathlib, re
p = pathlib.Path('dev/tools/preflight.ts'); s = p.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
start = s.index('/** Colour codes')
end = s.index('/**\n * Asks wrangler')
new = '''/**
 * The actual reason, out of wrangler's chatter. Colour codes, the version banner, the
 * telemetry notice and the log-file footer are all longer than the error on a bad day,
 * so they are dropped by name rather than by length.
 */
function firstUsefulLine(output: string): string {
  const noise = [
    /^Logs were written/,
    /rerun this command with/,
    /Cloudflare collects anonymous telemetry/,
    /^wrangler \\d/,
    /^[-\\u2500\\u2014\\s]*$/,
    /^\\[?(ERROR|WARNING)\\]?$/i,
  ];
  const lines = output
    // eslint-disable-next-line no-control-regex -- ANSI escapes are exactly what is being stripped
    .replace(/\\u001b\\[[0-9;]*m/g, '')
    .split('\\n')
    .map((line) => line.replace(/^[\\s\\u2718\\u25b2\\u26c5\\ufe0f]+/, '').trim())
    .map((line) => line.replace(/^\\[?(ERROR|WARNING)\\]?\\s*/i, ''))
    .filter((line) => line && !noise.some((pattern) => pattern.test(line)));
  const longest = lines.sort((a, b) => b.length - a.length)[0] ?? '';
  return longest.length > 200 ? `${longest.slice(0, 200)}…` : longest;
}

'''
p.write_text(s[:start] + new + s[end:], encoding='utf-8'); print('rewritten')

input.title: Add a deploy preflight and a post-deploy smoke test
input.body:
Two read-only tools around the deploy, and the workflow wiring for both. Closes the first half of #36; the preflight is the new gate on #27's first deploy.

## The preflight

`npm run preflight` answers one question — *does production exist yet* — and creates nothing, so it is safe to run repeatedly. It checks both secrets, both variables, the pinned `database_id`, and the existence of the D1 database, R2 bucket, queue, Pages project and (advisory, until #34) the Vectorize index.

The distinction it works hardest to keep is **missing** versus **unknown**: a resource Cloudflare told us is absent, against a question that could not be asked because the token is wrong, the command moved, or the network refused. Reporting the second as the first sends you to the dashboard to re-create something that is already there.

It is **staged**, and that matters: the origins cannot exist before the first deploy has happened, so a preflight that demanded them would deadlock the very deploy that creates them. `--stage resources` is everything that must exist beforehand and is what the deploy job runs; `--stage serving` is the origins.

## The smoke test

`npm run smoke` reads what actually shipped. Three probes:

1. `GET /api/v1/figures` returns 200 with an `items` array.
2. `GET /api/v1/nope` returns 404 with `error.code = "not_found"` — a parked domain or a platform placeholder passes probe 1 and fails this one, so this is what proves it is *our* Worker answering.
3. The site's root is the built index and carries the wordmark.

Each retries with backoff, because propagation delay is not a failed deploy.

## Both were exercised before landing

- **Preflight, no credentials** — every secret reported missing, every wrangler question reported unknown with its reason. This is also how the subcommand names were confirmed: they failed on *authentication*, not on "unknown command", which was the part I could not verify from docs.
- **Preflight, bad token** — the reason becomes the network failure, still unknown rather than missing.
- **Smoke, healthy deployment** — a real seeded Worker on `workerd` plus the built site on a static server: all three probes pass.
- **Smoke, origins swapped** — the classic misconfiguration. All three fail, each naming what it expected and what it got.

Getting the reason line right took three attempts: first line, longest line, and finally wrangler's own `✘` marker — position and length both pick the version banner, the proxy warning or the bug-report boilerplate depending on the day.

## One extra human step, and one made clearer

`SITE_ORIGIN` joins `API_ORIGIN` as a repository variable — the smoke test needs to know where the site landed, and scraping it out of deploy output is fragile. Both are set in the same visit, and the build step's failure message now says outright that this is the expected first-pass behaviour rather than leaving you to work it out.

## Folders touched

```
dev/tools/          preflight.ts and smoke.ts — the two read-only checks
.github/workflows/  preflight.yml (dispatchable, choose a stage); product.yml
                    gains a preflight before the deploy and a smoke test after it
```

Refs #27, #36

input.body:
Phase 0 of #25. Every step here needs the Cloudflare dashboard or the repo's secret store, so none of it can be done from a session — this is the checklist for whoever has those. The code that consumes each resource is written and its binding name is already fixed in `wrangler.toml`. Local development and the whole test suite run against wrangler's local D1/R2/Queues and need none of this: **what is blocked is production only.** **Consolidated 2026-08-22**, and updated when the preflight landed (#38). This body holds every step, in the order they have to happen; the ordering is load-bearing. **You do not have to guess whether a step worked.** After each one, run the **preflight** — Actions → *preflight* → Run workflow. It reads production and changes nothing, so run it as often as you like, and it names what is still missing. It is also the first thing to run if a deploy fails. --- ## A. Only a human can do these - [ ] **Pick the Cloudflare account**, and copy its Account ID. - [ ] **Create a scoped API token** with *Workers Scripts:Edit, D1:Edit, R2:Edit, Queues:Edit, Pages:Edit, Vectorize:Edit, Workers AI:Read*. - [ ] **Paste both as repository secrets**: `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` and `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → *Secrets*).
*While off:* the deploy job detects the missing credentials, says so, and exits clean. Nothing else in this list can be done either, because everything below needs the token. ## B. Create the resources Each one exists before the first deploy, because `wrangler deploy` fails when a binding names a resource that is not there — it does not create them for you. - [ ] **D1 database** `hitbut-corpus`.
*While off:* the Worker has no corpus; every API route 500s. - [ ] **R2 bucket** `hitbut-raw` (binding `RAW`).
*While off:* no raw-payload cache and no bulk NDJSON export; a parser fix would need a re-fetch. - [ ] **Queue** `hitbut-analysis` (producer + consumer, both already in `wrangler.toml`).
*While off:* acquisition cannot hand statements to analysis; nothing gets judged. - [ ] **Enable Workers AI** on the account (binding `AI`).
*While off:* analysis has no judge; pairs are drawn and never scored. - [ ] **Vectorize index** for utterance embeddings, bound as `VECTORS` (from #34). Its dimension count is fixed at creation and must match the chosen embedding model — **pick the model first**. The preflight reports this one as advisory until #34 lands.
*While off:* nothing can be clustered or compared by position; detection has no retrieval step and finds nothing. - [ ] **Enable Workflows** on the account (from #34).
*While off:* the historical backfill has no runtime. The moving-edge cron still works, so the site would carry only what was said after launch — which is the half of the product that is not the point. - [ ] **Pages project** named `hitbut`, no build command (CI uploads the built `dist/`). Create it explicitly rather than relying on the CLI to create it — a non-interactive runner cannot answer a prompt.
*While off:* there is no site. Note on models: the redesign needs **two** model calls of different shapes — an embedding model (one vector per utterance, high volume, cheap) and a stance model (one judgment per utterance, low volume, needs real Hebrew competence). They may not come from the same provider, and #28's item 3 — Hebrew competence unevaluated — applies to the second. ## C. One step lands as a commit, not a click - [ ] **Paste the real `database_id`** into the `[[d1_databases]]` block in `wrangler.toml`, replacing the all-zeros placeholder, and merge it.
*While off:* the migrate step runs against a database id that does not exist and the deploy fails on its first real step. ## D. Gate: preflight green before the first deploy - [ ] **Run the preflight at `resources` stage and get it green.** Everything above is exactly what it checks, and the deploy job runs the same check before it touches anything — so a green preflight is the difference between a first deploy that works and one that fails halfway through, having already deployed the Worker. Read its output carefully: `MISS` means Cloudflare says the resource is not there, `??` means the question could not be asked at all (usually a token scope). They need opposite fixes, and creating a resource that already exists because a `??` was read as a `MISS` is the mistake this distinction exists to prevent. ## E. The first deploy takes two passes, by design The site is static, so the API's origin is baked in at build time — and neither origin exists until things have been deployed once. So: - [ ] **Let the deploy run** (merging C is enough). It runs the preflight, applies the migrations and ships the Worker; the site build then fails, on purpose, with a message saying this is the expected first-pass behaviour. - [ ] **Set two repository variables** — Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → *Variables*, not Secrets: - `API_ORIGIN` — the deployed Worker's origin (`https://hitbut-api..workers.dev`, or the custom domain if you put one in front of it). - `SITE_ORIGIN` — where Pages put the site. The smoke test needs it, and reading it out of deploy output is fragile enough not to rely on. - [ ] **Re-run the `product` workflow** on `main` (Actions → product → Run workflow — `workflow_dispatch` is wired and the deploy job accepts it). This pass builds the site against the real origin, ships it, and then the **smoke test** fetches both and asserts they actually answer. Every deploy after this one is a single pass with no human step, which is requirement `7.1`. **Closes when** the `product` workflow on `main` is green end to end — including the smoke test — and one merge is observed reaching the deployed site with no human build step. #30 checks for exactly that and reports back on its own. Refs #25, #34, #36, #38 --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

The first half is built in #38 — `dev/tools/smoke.ts`, wired as the last step of the deploy job. Three probes, each retried with backoff: the API serves the corpus, the 404 envelope is ours (which is what distinguishes our Worker from a parked domain or a platform placeholder, since both pass the first probe), and the site is the built site carrying the wordmark.

It was exercised in both directions before landing — green against a real seeded Worker plus the built site, and red against those two origins swapped, with each probe naming what it expected and what it got.

**What remains here is the rollback path**, and it still needs Cloudflare's docs, which are unreachable from an agent session. Two pieces:

- Record the previous good deploy's version or deployment id in the job output, so the answer at 2am is a command rather than an investigation.
- Write down and exercise once the actual mechanism for both Workers and Pages.

Deliberately not automated: a smoke failure should stay loud rather than silently reverting. Automating the revert is worth considering only once the failure signal has been trusted for a while.

content.text:
Here's how deployments go, and what's actually yours to do.

**The steady state is nothing.** Merge to `main` → the fast lanes and the screen lane must pass → the deploy job applies migrations, deploys the Worker, builds the site against the API origin, deploys Pages, and now smoke-tests what shipped. No human step. That's requirement `7.1`, and [#30](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/30) checks weekly, on its own, that it's true.

**Getting to that steady state is a one-time sequence with two traps**, both now handled rather than left to be discovered:

The first is that **provisioning isn't purely dashboard work** — one step lands as a commit. `wrangler.toml` carries an all-zeros `database_id` placeholder, and the migrate step runs against whatever is there. So the checklist has a section C that produces a PR.

The second is that **the first deploy needs two passes, structurally**. The site is static, so the API's origin is compiled into the bundle — and that origin doesn't exist until the Worker has been deployed once. There's no clever way around it, so the deploy is now explicit about it: pass one ships the Worker and fails the site build with a message saying this is expected; you paste two variables; a re-run ships the site. Every deploy after that is one pass.

**Your steps, in order:** create the account and a scoped token, paste two secrets, create the six resources, paste the real `database_id` and merge it, run the preflight until it's green, let the deploy run, paste the two origins, re-run. # Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`), body ending `Closes #<issue>`.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.
6. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it again.
7. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.

{"id":32543978178,"name":"product","display_title":"Add a deploy preflight and a post-deploy smoke test","workflow_id":339572729,"run_number":4,"run_attempt":1,"event":"pull_request","status":"completed","conclusion":"failure","head_branch":"claude/hitbut-deploy-preflight","head_sha":"c71b7baf2e3f31f004ecd9d64456a66533d54a20","head_commit":{"message":"Add a deploy preflight and a post-deploy smoke test

Two reads, no writes. The preflight answers 'does production exist yet' — every
secret, variable, resource and the pinned database_id — and is safe to run any
number of times. It keeps missing and unknown apart: a resource Cloudflare says
is absent, versus a question we could not ask because the token is wrong or the
network refused. Reporting the second as the first sends someone to re-create
what is already there.

It is staged, because the origins cannot exist before the first deploy has
happened and gating that deploy on them would deadlock. The deploy job runs the
resources stage only; the standalone workflow runs whichever you ask for.

The smoke test reads what actually shipped. Everything the suite proves is
proven against a local workerd, so a missing binding, an unapplied migration or
a swapped origin is invisible to it and fatal in production. Three probes: the
API serves the corpus, the 404 envelope is ours (a parked domain returns 200 for
the first probe but not this one), and the site is the built site.

Both were exercised before landing: the preflight against no credentials and
against a bad token, which is also how its wrangler subcommand names were
confirmed; the smoke test against a real seeded Worker plus the built site, then
against those two origins swapped, where all three probes fail with the reason.

content.subject: Author dev/requirements/requirements.md (phase 1 spec)
content.description: Numbered leaves for corpus, search, acquisition, analysis, API, site. Spec-only commit, no code alongside (feature-requirements-first).

content.subject: Build the executable-requirements harness + coverage gate
content.description: Kind registry (logic/behavior/server/screen), case discovery, bijection gate, per-kind runners, gallery generator + gate, CI wiring. Watch the gate go red first.

content.subject: Shared contract + corpus store (phases 2-3)
content.description: src/shared types, D1 schema+migrations, ULID/slug ids, Hebrew-aware search indexing, supersede-not-delete invariants, logic cases.

content.subject: Acquisition + analysis (phases 4-5)
content.description: Shared fetch module (retry/backoff/bot-wall/raw-to-R2), source registry, queue consumer, pairing, judge interface + versioned prompt, behavior cases.

content.subject: HTTP API on the real Worker (phase 6)
content.description: /api/v1 routes, cursor pagination, CORS, read-only, NDJSON export; server-kind cases against the real handler under miniflare/wrangler.

content.subject: Preact+Vite RTL frontend + screen goldens (phase 7)
content.description: Six pages against /api/v1, warm-editorial RTL-first design system, vendored fonts, Playwright goldens against a local preview of the real deployment.

content.subject: Deploy plumbing + phase 0 hand-over issue (phases 0, 8)
content.description: wrangler config, deploy workflow from main, and the human-only Cloudflare provisioning checklist issue.
content.activeForm: Wiring deploy and filing the provisioning issue

The corpus becomes utterances with many attestations: one speech carried by
five outlets is one thing said and five documents reporting it, each with the
venue and the audience it reached. Without that split a persona is compared
against themselves and every echo reads as agreement. Dates carry a precision,
because thirty years back a source often establishes a month and no more.

Analysis stops judging pairs. Subjects are discovered by embedding rather than
declared as a topic list, and because embedding distance measures aboutness and
not agreement, a second cheap step places each utterance on its cluster's axis.
That gives a stance series per persona per subject, in which an anomaly is a
deviation (and the venue is the interesting part) and a trend change is a
change point (and the date is). Pairwise judging was O(n^2), needed a topic
vocabulary to stay survivable, and could not see a trend at all.

The historical backfill becomes a Workflow driven per archive slice, sharing
the Worker's ingestion code. Cloudflare's step and duration limits could not be
read from this environment, so the doc marks that assumption unverified rather
than asserting numbers.

Two reads, no writes. The preflight answers 'does production exist yet' — every
secret, variable, resource and the pinned database_id — and is safe to run any
number of times. It keeps missing and unknown apart: a resource Cloudflare says
is absent, versus a question we could not ask because the token is wrong or the
network refused. Reporting the second as the first sends someone to re-create
what is already there.

It is staged, because the origins cannot exist before the first deploy has
happened and gating that deploy on them would deadlock. The deploy job runs the
resources stage only; the standalone workflow runs whichever you ask for.

The smoke test reads what actually shipped. Everything the suite proves is
proven against a local workerd, so a missing binding, an unapplied migration or
a swapped origin is invisible to it and fatal in production. Three probes: the
API serves the corpus, the 404 envelope is ours (a parked domain returns 200 for
the first probe but not this one), and the site is the built site.

Both were exercised before landing: the preflight against no credentials and
against a bad token, which is also how its wrangler subcommand names were
confirmed; the smoke test against a real seeded Worker plus the built site, then
against those two origins swapped, where all three probes fail with the reason.

The corpus becomes utterances with many attestations: one speech carried by
five outlets is one thing said and five documents reporting it, each with the
venue and the audience it reached. Without that split a persona is compared
against themselves and every echo reads as agreement. Dates carry a precision,
because thirty years back a source often establishes a month and no more.

Analysis stops judging pairs. Subjects are discovered by embedding rather than
declared as a topic list, and because embedding distance measures aboutness and
not agreement, a second cheap step places each utterance on its cluster's axis.
That gives a stance series per persona per subject, in which an anomaly is a
deviation (and the venue is the interesting part) and a trend change is a
change point (and the date is). Pairwise judging was O(n^2), needed a topic
vocabulary to stay survivable, and could not see a trend at all.

The historical backfill becomes a Workflow driven per archive slice, sharing
the Worker's ingestion code. Cloudflare's step and duration limits could not be
read from this environment, so the doc marks that assumption unverified rather
than asserting numbers.

I'm holding the merge. Here's why, with the evidence.

**Every workflow in the repo has been failing since roughly midnight UTC, and none of it is this PR.**

The `Claudinite scheduler` runs hourly on `main` at sha `25f8e07`. That exact sha, that exact workflow, succeeded at 23:02 and has failed on **every run since 00:01** — fourteen consecutive failures. Nothing about `main` changed in between. PR [#35](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/pull/35) went fully green at 23:14; [#38](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/pull/38) at 01:37 failed all three jobs, including `claudinite-sweeps`, which my diff doesn't touch.

The signature is unmistakable: jobs start and die after 2–3 seconds, produce **no retrievable logs** (the API 404s on them), and it hits every workflow regardless of content — even the `report-failure` job whose only purpose is to report the failure. That isn't a test failing. That's jobs being killed before they run.

This is almost certainly account-level rather than code-level — Actions minutes exhausted or a spending limit reached on a private repo, or Actions disabled. I can't see billing from here, so I can't confirm which. Worth checking, in order: repo **Settings → Actions** (is it still enabled), then your account **Settings → Billing** for Actions minutes and any spending limit.

Two things follow from that, and I'd rather flag them than let them sit:

**Your Claudinite automation has been dead for fourteen hours.** The hourly scheduler is how queued work gets picked up, so nothing has been running.

**I did not merge #38.** The merge procedure waits for checks to pass, and these are red on the base branch too — which is precisely the case where pushing a "fix" would be wrong, since there's nothing in the diff to fix. The local suite is green (35 tests, plus the server and screen lanes), and both new tools were exercised in both directions before I pushed, so I have good evidence the change is sound — I just can't get CI's word for it.

options.description: Leave it open. Once Actions runs again, the checks re-run and I merge on green. Costs nothing but time, and keeps the rule that main only takes verified changes — which matters more now that main is the deploy trigger.

options.label: Merge it now anyway
options.description: The full suite passes locally and both tools were exercised in both directions. Your call to make, not mine — but it puts a change on main that CI never checked, at a moment when you cannot tell a real failure from the outage.

options.label: Hold, and re-run the checks once you have fixed billing
options.description: Same as holding, but I re-trigger the workflow myself when you tell me Actions is back, rather than waiting for a push to do it.

options.description: Add utterances, attestations and date precision alongside the existing statements — nothing removed, everything still green — following the expand/migrate/contract discipline #37 asks for. Lands as its own PR, verifiable locally even while CI is down.

options.label: The rollback half of #36
options.description: The other half of the deploy safety net. Blocked on Cloudflare's docs, which are unreachable from this sandbox, so parts would be written blind and would need your verification before they could be trusted.

options.label: Nothing until CI is back
options.description: Wait. Avoids stacking a third unreviewed PR on top of two already open, and avoids building on a redesign (#35) you have not approved yet.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.
